title: Multidimensional Analysis of Chlamydia Test Uptake in Women Aged 16 to 25
summary: Chlamydia infections are among the most common sexually transmitted infections in Germany. Women up to the age of 25 have had a statutory right to free annual screening since 2007. However, this offer has so far failed to reach the target group adequately. The FemScreen-CT project investigates why the screening is used too infrequently and how this can be improved. To this end, a multi-method approach is used in which young women (aged 16–25) and office-based gynaecologists are surveyed, statutory health insurance claims data are analysed, and a health economic assessment is conducted. The surveys are developed on the basis of insights from focus groups with the target group and subject matter experts. All findings will be brought together at the end of the project in practice-oriented recommendations for action, which will be developed in consensus with relevant stakeholders.
conditions: Genital Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) infections in asymptomatic women aged 15–25 years; uptake of the statutory chlamydia screening programme in Germany

interventions.name: WP1: WP1.1 Anonymous, asynchronous, chat-app-based online focus group. WP1.2: Quantitative cross-sectional survey study (online) of sexually active women aged 16 to 25 years. WP1.3: Analysis of usage statistics of an online application for anonymous sexual partner notification.
WP2: Secondary data analysis of statutory health insurance (KV) claims data
WP3: Quantitative cross-sectional survey study (postal) of office-based gynaecologists
WP4: Health economic modelling based on existing evidence and results from AP2 and AP3
WP5: Participatory development of recommendations for action based on the findings from AP1 to AP4

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
AP1.1: A smartphone, tablet, or computer with internet access is required.
AP1.2: Memberhsip in one of the three cooperating health insurance funds. Additional criteria:
• A: Women aged 16–25 with consultation code GOP 01821 and GOP 01822
• B: Women aged 16–25 with consultation code GOP 01821 or GOP 01822 and GOP 01823 (supplement to GOP 01821 and GOP 01822 for counselling on CT screening)
• C: Women aged 16–25 with consultation code GOP 01821 or GOP 01822 and GOP 01840 and GOP 01824 (initiation of urine sample analysis for Chlamydia trachomatis, result negative (no chlamydia diagnosis according to ICD-10: A56.-))
• D: Women aged 16–25 with a positive chlamydia test according to ICD-10, A56.- (chlamydial diseases transmitted by sexual intercourse)
AP1.3: Women from selection group D.
AP3: Only physicians working in a gynaecological practice are included.
Exclusion criteria:
None
